subject: ISO/FedRAMP audit: sample strategy, evidence scaling, and owner confirmations
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, AuditOps <auditops@thirdparty-audit.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ISO/FedRAMP audit: sample strategy & evidence scaling

Team / AuditOps —

Following up from last week's intake, I want to align on a pragmatic sample strategy and evidence scale for the upcoming ISO 27001 scoping review and our initial FedRAMP readiness intake. High-level asks below and a draft evidence request attached.

Summary / proposal:
- Scope: controls in scope for FedRAMP impact boundary v1.1 — infra (GCP us-east1), control plane (Redwood console), and customer-facing inference endpoints.
- Sample approach: start with 10% tenant sample (min 5 tenants, max 20) for configuration and retention artifacts; increase to 20% if we need more coverage for multi-tenant access controls. AuditOps: can you confirm whether 10% aligns with auditor expectations for readiness windows?
- Evidence scale: prioritize syslog retention, key management attestations (KMS artifacts), access review certs, and change-control PRs for kernel/serving changes.
- Owners: I propose Mina as lead for evidence intake, Vanessa for control mapping signoff, Markus for infra artifacts. Please confirm or reassign.

Attachments: control-mapping.xlsx (draft), evidence-request-draft.pdf

Next steps / asks (actionable):
1) AuditOps: confirm sample size range and any documentation templates you require (CAIQ/SIG preferences).
2) Mina: can you pull a list of candidate tenants for sampling by EOD Monday (2026-07-20)? Include environment, region, and last activity date.
3) Vanessa: recommend any changes to control mapping sheet by Monday — I want signoff on in-scope controls before we send to auditors.
4) Markus: start scoping logs and retention artifacts; note any operational blockers for producing 13 months of historical logs (if needed).

I'll consolidate replies and issue a single evidence ask packet and a Jira epic for tracking.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

-----Original Attachment: evidence-request-draft.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, AuditOps <auditops@thirdparty-audit.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ISO/FedRAMP audit: sample strategy & evidence scaling

Jonas — thanks for the clear ask. A few clarifying questions and quick flags from my side: 

1) Tenant sampling: for the candidate list I'll need the definition of "tenant" we're using (org-level vs project-level). For previous SOC work we sampled at org-level — just want to be explicit.
2) Logs: we can produce aggregated request logs and KV cache access logs, but per-tenant retention for 13 months requires pulling from cold storage snapshots. That will add ~24-48 hours of engineering time per snapshot request. Markus — can ops confirm estimated lead time?
3) Evidence format: do auditors want CSV manifests for each artifact (preferred) or will PDF exports be acceptable? CSV makes programmatic verification easier.
4) Control owners: I suggest adding Priya as owner for key management artifacts (Priya Natarajan) — she's on-call for KMS rotations.

I'm attaching a short checklist of artifacts I'll collect first pass in order of priority: access reviews, IAM role bindings, KMS rotation logs, PR change history for serving runtime, and retention policy docs.

Mina
Sr. Manager, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ISO/FedRAMP audit: sample strategy & evidence scaling

Jonas / team —

Thanks for the outline and attachments — that is helpful. Quick responses to your asks: 

- Sample size: 10% tenant sample (min 5 / max 20) is acceptable for an initial readiness review. If evidence sampling shows high variance across tenants we'll ask to expand to 20%.
- Evidence templates: CAIQ + SIG are fine, and we prefer CSV manifests for artifact inventories. Please include a mapping doc that ties each artifact to the control ID (e.g., ISO A.9.2 -> access review.csv).
- Logs: auditors expect retention proof for the claimed period. If you must pull from cold snapshots, list expected lead time and any costs.
- Additional asks: a completed CAIQ for your current control baseline; a copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type II if available; and the audit-intake-form (attached) — please return within 10 business days.

Attached: audit-intake-form.pdf (populated by us for your signature)

We will tentatively book a 90-minute intake call the week of 2026-07-27 to walk through the mapping and sample list. Please propose 2x 90-minute slots.

Regards,
AuditOps Intake Team
ThirdParty Audit Services

-----Attachment: audit-intake-form.pdf (PDF stub)

Thanks all — good alignment. Finalizing owners and deadlines below (I'll create the Jira epic JIRA-SEC-8421 and upload artifacts to the Drive link):

Action items (owners / deadlines):
- Evidence intake & tenant list (Mina) — candidate list by 2026-07-20 EOD; manifest CSVs for first 5 tenants by 2026-07-27.
- Control mapping signoff (Vanessa) — review + signoff on mapping sheet by 2026-07-21. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2C3D_ISO-FedRAMP-Prep
- Infra artifacts & logs lead time (Markus) — confirm snapshot lead time and estimated engineering hours by 2026-07-20.
- CAIQ + SOC2 delivery (AuditOps request) — AuditOps: please confirm the preferred return format for CAIQ (we'll aim CSV + PDF).
- Engagement letter & scoping (Jonas) — I'll route the audit intake form for signature and post the DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/envelope/abc123

Notes / risks:
- If cold snapshots are required for >6 tenants, expect a 5-7 business day delay for full artifact collection. We should surface this to procurement and customer success if it impacts SLA windows.
- We may need a small budget for snapshot retrieval if it exceeds standard ops runbook allowances; I'll prepare a short memo for finance if that becomes necessary.

I'll follow up with the Jira epic and an ETA update tomorrow.

Jonas Weber
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
